Score cut 8 to 6: real unfired contractual gate with clean provenance and genuine residual, but this is a differentiated-view merger-arb bet on regulator discretion, not an unpriced catalyst, and every piece of primary evidence since August points the wrong way.

G3 FAIL (no specific currently-unpriced figure; the flagged upside traces to a 2026-09-04 Canaccord Genuity initiation target, not to a re-derived number, and ~$7.0B of the $7.76B market cap is already pre-approval option value).
verified.edge: L. Run-up: +163% from the pre-readout base ($73.50 on 2025-10-01) and +65% from $117 (2025-11-10, before the DRAGON Phase 3 ramp) to $193.61; +15.8% from the NDA-acceptance eve ($167.26 on 2026-08-10). verified.primary_source: Belite Bio press release / GlobeNewswire, "FDA Acceptance and Priority Review of NDA for Tinlarebant," 2026-08-11 (PDUFA 2027-02-12), filed as 6-K (SEC CIK 0001889109); Benzinga 2026-09-04 "Why Is Belite Bio Stock Soaring Friday?" (Canaccord Genuity initiation = the +13.2% move); FMP quote 2026-09-04 ($193.61, mcap $7.76B) and Q2-2026 balance sheet (2026-06-30).
verified.analysis: The catalyst is genuine, dated, specific and forward — the FDA accepted the tinlarebant NDA on 2026-08-11 under priority review with a 2027-02-12 action date, and approval would be the first therapy ever cleared for Stargardt disease type 1 — so G1 and G2 clear cleanly and this is in no sense a macro bet. But it fails on residual capture and on the re-rate test: the +13.2% move the triage cited was a Canaccord Genuity initiation on 2026-09-04, not new company or agency information, and the actual FDA news four weeks earlier produced only a +6% one-day pop that fully faded within two sessions ($167.26 to $178.94 to $162.80 by 08-14) — direct tape evidence that the market had already discounted approval before the announcement. The stock is +163% from $73.50 (2025-10-01) and sits at $193.61 against a $200 52-week high, with the balance sheet clean enough that no waterfall haircut applies but also offering no support: $777M of book equity against a $7.76B cap means ~$7.0B is pre-approval option value on a single orphan asset whose own indication math tops out near $5-6B. Score capped at 4 under the mostly-harvested rule — a real, near-certain, entirely unfired event where the gain has already been taken and the flagged upside is an inherited sell-side target rather than a re-derived figure. Gap to note: I did not verify the exact DRAGON topline announcement date or a management-guided peak-sales figure within the lookup budget, so the pre-catalyst base is inferred from the price series rather than pinned to a press release.

NEXT DATE: Banco Santander extraordinary general meeting to approve the capital increase funding the offer - not yet called as of the 14-Aug-2026 Form 425, expected to be scheduled in Q4-2026; then F-4 effectiveness and formal offer launch, with Brazilian (CVM/BACEN) and US regulatory approvals, and completion guided to H1-2027 (no fixed outside date disclosed).
verified.instrument: Ratio trade only: long BSBR vs short 0.4056 SAN per share. Outright long BSBR is a Santander-beta position, not an arb - since 31-Jul BSBR trades as a fixed-ratio SAN tracker.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 PASS - named counterparty is the parent, Banco Santander SA, in its own 30-Jul-2026 press release and BSBR Form 425 (SEC, 14-Aug-2026). G2 PASS - concrete commitment: fixed exchange ratio 0.4056 SAN BDR/ADS per BSBR unit/ADS, ~EUR1,908M maximum consideration, ~15% premium to the reference price. G3 FAIL - there is no specific currently-unpriced figure; the entire un-captured quantum is a 1.6% residual spread, which is not an unpriced number, it is a closed arb.
verified.edge: L. RESIDUAL CAPTURE, ratio-adjusted (mandatory since this is stock-for-stock, so raw price run-up double-counts SAN beta): pre-catalyst base 30-Jul-2026 BSBR $5.05 / SAN $14.11 = ratio 0.3579 vs the contractual 0.4056, i.e. a 13.3% premium on announcement. (a) RUN-UP: headline BSBR $5.05 -> $5.96 = +18.0%, of which SAN itself contributed +5.8% ($14.11 -> $14.93); the event-attributable ratio re-rate is 0.3579 -> 0.3992 = +11.5%, so 11.5 of the 13.3pp premium is gone = ~87% HARVESTED, and 12.3pp of it fired in a single session on 31-Jul-2026. (b) REMAINING: deal value today = 0.4056 x $14.93 = $6.06 vs BSBR $5.96 = +1.60% gross to a H1-2027 close (~9 months) = ~2.1% annualized, below the risk-free rate and negative after SAN borrow and the ADS/BDR conversion friction. Asymmetry is inverted: a break reverts the ratio to 0.3579 = $5.34 at today's SAN, so risk/reward is +$0.10 against -$0.62 = 0.16x. This is buying the receipt, not the gain.
verified.primary_source: Banco Santander press release, "Santander announces its intention to launch an exchange offer to acquire the outstanding shares of Santander Brazil," 30-Jul-2026 (santander.com), corroborated by Banco Santander (Brasil) S.A. Form 425 filed with the SEC 14-Aug-2026 (accession 000129281426004260) and Form 6-K 30-Jul-2026; prices from FMP batch-quote and EOD history as of the 05-Sep-2026 close.
verified.analysis: The event is genuinely real, dated and forward - the offer has not launched, the SAN capital-increase EGM has not been called as of the 14-Aug-2026 Form 425, and completion is guided to H1-2027 - but it is also ~87% harvested, which is the only question that matters here. BSBR closed the ratio gap to 99% of parity on the first session after the 30-Jul-2026 announcement and now trades as a fixed-ratio SAN tracker with 1.60% left to a nine-month close, against a 10.4% give-back if the offer fails; the structure removes every mechanism that normally pays the last few points, because there is no minimum acceptance condition, no delisting is sought, and there is no cash floor or appraisal backstop, so no forced-seller squeeze and weak pressure for a bump. Numerator provenance: the $6.06 is re-derived mechanically from the contractual 0.4056 ratio times SAN's live $14.93 (a stock-for-stock ratio is contractual and exempt from the SoP waterfall re-derivation), not inherited from any analyst target - the triage note's "thin asymmetry" read was directionally right but understated it, since the residual is not merely thin, it is sub-riskfree with a negative expected value at a break probability above ~2.5%. Watch only for a spread blowout (SAN rallying while BSBR lags, or a bump attached to the EGM), not as an entry today.
